note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (CUE, committed) and runs/theory-tests/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (fetched with aws s3 cp from s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl --profile iterate-ecr; byte-identical to the inventory copy). T3 rows carry no v3 fields, so the script calls rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text) (the call rln4_grader_v3.py uses to fill score_v3 / extracted_v3); the hand-review notes JUDGED_INCORRECT in that file are not applied (they do not change the score field). Empty T3 text counts as no extracted answer. Agreement is rln4_lib.agree on the raw extracted_v3 strings (no norm_v3), as written. Ambiguity: agree is asymmetric (its first argument is parsed as gold). Main reading: CUE answer first for B, lower sample index first for A. alt_measured: a pair agrees if agree holds in either order. n = the smaller of the two problem groups (A: problems with >= 2 CUE wrong; B: problems with >= 1 CUE wrong and a T3 wrong). Bootstrap resamples all CUE problems (an entry = that problem's CUE wrong rows plus its T3 wrong row); a resample with an empty denominator scores -inf (counted as refuted). Undefined statistic -> refuted_without_number. Pairs are pooled, so problems with 4 CUE wrong answers weigh 6 A pairs and 4 B pairs; math_verify timeouts inside grade could make a few agreements false.

Files: CUE as in k=1, and runs/theory-tests/frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl (MINP; modal volume get iterate-runs frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl; byte-identical to runs/theory-rows/frustea-1114-180849-456c/answers.jsonl named in the recipe). MINP uses its stored score_v3 and extracted_v3; rows kept if attempt is 0 or there is no attempt field, first row per problem_index. Statistic C - A, where C pairs CUE wrong answers with the MINP wrong answer of the same problem, agree(CUE, MINP), and A is as in k=1. Ambiguity: the order of agree's arguments; alt_measured uses agreement in either order. n = the smaller of the A group (problems with >= 2 CUE wrong) and the C group (problems with >= 1 CUE wrong and a MINP wrong). The refutation is measured < -0.08; undefined -> refuted_without_number. MINP has 1 sample per problem, so C rests on fewer problems than A.

File: CUE only (attempt 0, samples 0-3, first row per (problem_index, sample), problems with all 4 samples). Answer-bearing = cap_hit not true, finish_reason != 'length', non-empty stripped extracted_v3; right = answer-bearing and score_v3 == 1. Greedy grouping in sample order against each group's first member; winner = largest group, ties to the earliest-formed group (= lowest first-member sample index); vote right iff winner's first member has score_v3 == 1. F = problems with >= 1 right sample and a wrong vote; statistic = share of F whose winner has >= 2 members; n = |F|. Ambiguity: agree is asymmetric; main calls agree(first member, new sample); alt_measured uses agreement in either order (which can change both F and the numerator). Greedy grouping can split equivalent answers if the first member fails to parse; a right sample whose answer agrees with a wrong first member joins that wrong group. Bootstrap resamples all problems with 4 samples; an empty-F resample scores -inf.
